title: The Crown of the Weeping Wood
premise: In the city of Vell, where magic was outlawed a generation ago, Felix Galloway survives by stealing memories and bottling them as harmless charms. When the crown's witch-hunters begin burning the gifted in the square, Felix learns that their own sister's soul was sold fifteen years ago to the court beneath the mountain—a fae kingdom that trades in what mortals surrender. To save her before her soul is fully consumed at the turning of the year, Felix must ally with a disgraced witch-hunter, a memoryless noblewoman, and the very memories they once sold. In the end, Felix discovers the court's queen is the stolen soul of the city's founder, and can only defeat her by giving up their own most treasured memory—choosing truth over the self they built to survive.
about_author: S. M. Coldharbour is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated letters in a northern county records office before turning to fiction. They write about memory, exile, and the small magics people hide to stay alive.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller
chapters.summary: Felix Galloway works the night market of Vell, selling bottled memories disguised as luck-charms while hiding their gift from the wardens. A desperate mother buys a memory of her dead son, and Felix feels both purpose and shame. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: the quiet ache of belonging nowhere.

chapters.title: Ash on the Wind
chapters.summary: The crown proclaims a hunt for all gifted citizens; the first pyre burns in Founder's Square. Felix watches a neighbor dragged away and realizes their invisibility has an expiration date. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: fear hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Keeps
chapters.summary: Searching their late mentor's effects, Felix finds a ledger recording a sale: a child's soul sold to the court beneath the mountain fifteen years ago—their sister Wren. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: grief and guilt colliding.

chapters.title: The Hunter Who Wept
chapters.summary: Witch-hunter Captain Ilsa Verrow catches Felix mid-theft but hesitates to arrest them, haunted by the executions she's ordered. She offers an uneasy bargain instead. POV: alternating Felix and Ilsa. Emotional beat: enemies recognizing each other's wounds.

chapters.title: A Lady Without Yesterdays
chapters.summary: Felix seeks out Odile Marchand, a noblewoman who sold her entire past to pay a family debt and now hires Felix to steal back even one memory. She becomes an unlikely ally. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: two kinds of emptiness meeting.

chapters.title: The Road Under the Roots
chapters.summary: The three travel toward the mountain gate, guided by a bottled memory of the old roads. Wardens patrol the passes; Ilsa must use her authority to get them through. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: loyalty beginning to shift from crown to companions.

chapters.title: Toll of Small Things
chapters.summary: At the threshold, the mountain demands payment: each traveler surrenders a memory to enter. Felix pays with the memory of their mother's face. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: the cost of love made literal.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Felix descends into a glittering subterranean court where the fae nobility wear mortals' surrendered years like jewelry. They glimpse a girl with Wren's eyes serving the queen. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into horror.

chapters.title: The Queen's Kindness
chapters.summary: Queen Marenthe receives Felix with unsettling warmth, offering Wren's freedom in exchange for a service: steal a specific memory from the surface world. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: Bargains and Blind Spots
chapters.summary: Odile warns that the queen's bargains always conceal a second price; Ilsa argues for taking the deal to save Wren now. The alliance fractures. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: trust tested by desperation.

chapters.title: The Memory Vault
chapters.summary: Felix infiltrates the court's vault where souls are stored as light in glass, and finds Wren's soul already half-consumed—and beside it, a vial labeled with the founder's name. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into questions.

chapters.title: Wren, Almost
chapters.summary: Felix reaches Wren's body, hollowed and dreamlike; she remembers nothing of him but hums their childhood song. He realizes he cannot simply take her and run. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: heartbreak without catharsis.

chapters.title: The Hunter's Confession
chapters.summary: Ilsa reveals she signed the order that condemned Wren's family fifteen years ago under pressure from the crown. She offers her own life as forfeit. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: guilt seeking absolution and finding only responsibility.

chapters.title: What the Founder Buried
chapters.summary: Odile recovers a fragment of her past revealing the truth: Queen Marenthe is the stolen soul of Vell's founder, sustained by centuries of sold souls—including Wren's. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Deep Roads
chapters.summary: Exposed, the three flee the court through collapsing deep roads as the queen's huntsmen pursue. Odile is wounded holding a passage open. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: loyalty forged under fire.

chapters.title: The Turning of the Year
chapters.summary: They surface with days left before the solstice, when Wren's soul will be fully consumed and the queen made unkillable. Vell's hunt has intensified in their absence. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: time running out like sand through fingers.

chapters.title: City of Informants
chapters.summary: Back in Vell, Felix rallies the hidden gifted—the charm-sellers, hedge-healers, and memory-thieves—together for the first time. Some refuse; one betrays them. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: belonging finally offered, and its risks.

chapters.title: The Betrayal
chapters.summary: Ilsa is arrested for treason after the informant names her; the crown announces her execution at the solstice—same hour, same square. Felix must choose between Wren and Ilsa. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: sacrifice offered without expectation.

chapters.title: Two Fires, One Night
chapters.summary: On solstice eve, the gifted split: some free Ilsa from the pyre while Felix descends alone to the mountain with the founder's vial. The plan half-collapses. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: courage that costs everything.

chapters.title: The Crown of the Weeping Wood
chapters.summary: In the court's heart, Felix confronts Queen Marenthe, who wears the weeping wood of the founder's memory as her crown. She offers Felix everything they've ever wanted—if they surrender Wren's soul willingly. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: the climax of every temptation at once.

chapters.title: The Price of Truth
chapters.summary: Felix shatters the founder's vial, releasing the queen's original soul, and gives up their own most treasured memory—the day they learned their gift—to anchor Wren's return. The court begins to crumble. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: loss transfigured into love.

chapters.title: Morning in Vell
chapters.summary: Wren wakes whole but doesn't know Felix; Ilsa resigns her commission to help rebuild a city where magic might be lawful again; Odile chooses not to reclaim her past. Felix, lighter and stranger, plants a seed from the weeping wood. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: bittersweet belonging, finally earned.
